Latest Update: Conformity, Individuality, and the Lawns of Levittown

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (486 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a few miles from my home is historic Levittown, Long Island, where immediately after WWII, 4,000 acres of potato fields were plowed under to mass-produce more than 17,000 detached houses; many of these four-and-a-half-room homes were constructed in about two days.
  • Selling for less than $8,000 ($115,000 in 2024 dollars), each house came with a TV set and hi-fi.
  • A popular folksong tagged Levittown and other such developments as places of little boxes “made out of ticky tacky/And they all look the same.” No longer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

Just a few miles from my home is historic Levittown, Long Island, where immediately after WWII, 4,000 acres of potato fields were plowed under to mass-produce more than 17,000 detached houses; many of these four-and-a-half-room homes were constructed in about two days.

Selling for less than $8,000 ($115,000 in 2024 dollars), each house came with a TV set and hi-fi. Buyers could choose a red, yellow, or blue house in one of three styles, in neighborhoods largely devoid of trees. This first modern suburb prompted historian Lewis Mumford to describe Levittown as “a uniform environment from which escape is impossible.”.

A popular folksong tagged Levittown and other such developments as places of little boxes “made out of ticky tacky/And they all look the same.” No longer.

In a recent development, drive through the area today, and it is nearly impossible to imagine the architectural conformity that it once was. What is striking about Levittown is that as houses aged, they became distinctive from one another and went decidedly upscale. They expanded upward and sideways. These four-and-a-half-room homes now are four- or five-bedroom houses with two baths. Barren landscapes are long gone. In 2024, Levittown houses were listed in the $700,000 range.

The sterile 1950s transformed into the turbulent '60s, with subsequent decades bringing tremendous social change in their wake. Fresh generations moved in with new ideas; they had more money than did the returning war veterans. With time, Levittown’s appearance reflected the tastes of new homeowners.

Levittown reflects two contradictory impulses in human nature: The individuality impulse on the one hand, and conformity on the other. It is the universal desire to be recognized as a unique individual but at the same time desiring to be part of a group. The distinctiveness of the home displays this while adhering to the idealized standard of a suburban front lawn. You can drive for miles through Levittown—and almost every suburban neighborhood—and find that while the houses are no longer alike, not a single house has dispensed with grass lawns.

This would be a landscaping choice if it didn’t also mean that, to maintain the carpet-like appearance, the air is polluted with the fumes of mowers, the groundwater is poisoned with fertilizers (Long Island depends exclusively on its aquifer for its drinking water), and a din created by leaf blowers makes a quiet summer day around the house a rare event. Dispensing with lawns will probably have to be a policy decision, as there is only so much individuality that a person can express without feeling like an outsider. The change will have to come as an imposed municipal edict; not having a manicured lawn becomes a new enforced norm, where conformity becomes not having a grassy lawn.

  • It has been revealed that “His family was all on board with it,” current wing commander and retired pilot Rob Jenner told St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 85 years have passed since the very first B-25 bombers rolled off the assembly line. The legendary, twin-engine aircraft flew above every theater of World War II, and were instrumental to the Allied forces’ victory. Many B-25 bombers are preserved in museums, but a handful of them actually remain flightworthy today.

One of those flight-ready B25s is a plane nicknamed Show Me. The aircraft belongs to the Missouri Wing of the Commemorative Air Force, and has taken to the sky every fall since 2009 to demonstrate its impressive aerial bombardment capabilities. But Show Me doesn’t unleash an arsenal of destruction anymore. Instead, the B25 releases a bevy of hollowed-out pumpkins filled with red, white, and blue pool chalk. However, aircraft recently dropped more than gourds for onlookers outside St. Louis. During this year’s flight, Show Me also deployed a pumpkin stuffed with the ashes of the Missouri Wing’s late, beloved volunteer, Lou Tacchi, Jr.

It has been revealed that “His family was all on board with it,” current wing commander and retired pilot Rob Jenner told St. Louis public radio. “They had shirts printed up, and they called it the ‘Pop Drop.’”.

In a recent development, some of Tacchi, Jr.’s ashes were also packed away inside four .50-caliber shells that will now remain aboard the B-25. According to Jenner, their departed colleague will “fly with us forever,” thanks to his final request.

In a recent development, “[He] had such a deep interest in history, as well as the airplanes, and it was so much a part of his life,” Jenner added. “I think it was natural for him to pick that way to say goodbye.”.

Industry observers note that before it received its nickname, Show Me, the B-25 was simply classified by the United States Air Force as 44-31385. It first took to the sky in January 1945 and was used as a trainer for fresh pilots. Show me is technically a B-25J—the final variant of the aircraft which also featured an eight-gun strafer nose.

The military retired 44-31385 at Arizona’s Davis Monthan Air Force Base in 1958, before selling it to its first private owner the following year. A windstorm damaged the bomber a decade later while it was stored in Seymour, Illinois. Show Me remained grounded in Seymour until it was finally repaired in 1975. The Commemorative Air Force’s Missouri Wing received the B-25 in 1982.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a newly introduced update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the latest patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Industry observers note that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

According to recent reports, the Ice Climbing Axe is the only latest weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

According to recent reports, easily the most interesting change in this enhancement is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Recent findings suggest that some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this upgrade is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Industry observers note that speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

In a recent development, 1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

According to recent reports, something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an revision. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the glitch should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, has lost her seat.

Industry observers note that enhancement: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. After a recount, Chuck Hubbard has defeated Virginia Foxx by 330 votes, and will go on to represent NC-5 in Congress.

It has been revealed that christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Industry observers note that foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

It has been revealed that for the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get, but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

In a recent development, christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who remarked “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”.

It has been revealed that but then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily noted Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”.

I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

Recent findings suggest that foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.

Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.

In the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones. Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”.

Recent findings suggest that foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.

But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.

Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘new’ electric cars.”.

But she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just new ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.

Foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites. Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China. Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans.

Those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive, which is to say it reduced the national debt (by $238B), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.

According to recent reports, but most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.

In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.

But I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.

In a recent development, he will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024, from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change. Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.

Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess reveals where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.

Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and presently sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.

When we first wrote this article in May, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024.

But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.

After a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide, bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.

Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.

And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district, after winning by 330 votes in a recount.

The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats.

Generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.

Sources indicate that so they engaged in Gerrymandering, a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.

According to recent reports, foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.

But it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired. Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “Dummymander“. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems).

It has been revealed that after a nail-bitingly close election, Foxx requested a recount. The margin is extremely thin, just 0.12% of votes, but today Foxx called to concede, making it the last decided House race of the election, giving Democrats a 258-seat majority.

Industry observers note that foxx previously vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

In a recent development, A Mercedes-Benz executive coupe from the early 1990s is a grand tourer par excellence, and you could hardly do better than this well-traveled machine. Presently on Bring a Trailerr (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos), this is a European-spec 1991 560SEC that was imported first to Japan before being brought to the United States seven years ago. The mileage is reasonable at the equivalent of 78K miles, but if you like to travel, here's your beast.

According to recent reports, this generation of Mercedes coupe was the two-door sibling to the wunderbar W126 S-class, designed by the legendary Bruno Sacco. The first of these C126 coupes rolled out in 1981, kicking off a decade-long run that ended with the 1991 model year. These are truly great cars from the brand’s “The best or nothing” era.

See all results for used cars for sale near 29405.

U.S.-market 560s came with a fairly emissions-strangled version of Mercedes's 5.5-liter V-8, but this car benefits from higher compression and slightly freer-flowing exhaust. There were more powerful versions available, but here you can expect around 275 horsepower and mountains of creamy torque, fed through a four-speed automatic gearbox.

Industry observers note that it's not an AMG under the hood, nor are the stately looks here anywhere near as boisterous as the wide-body versions of the 560SEC that Affalterbach dreamed up. Here, the tailoring is more discreet, set off by a set of 17-inch Lorinser wheels and a slightly lower ride height on H&R springs with Bilstein dampers up front.

It looks understated and reserved in a way Mercedes doesn't really do anymore. Inside, it's just as cushy as you would hope, with leather heated seats, plenty of wood trim, and a stereo that has been updated with Bluetooth connectivity.

There’s an problem with the air conditioning that a specialist could probably address, but this example has had plenty of mechanical work done. The fuel system was overhauled with upcoming injectors and a new distributor a few years ago, and larger work including valve seals and a new timing chain was done two years ago. At that time, perishables like vacuum lines were also replaced.

Basically, this well-fettled significant coupe is an idealized version of the top-dog Mercedes from the brand’s glory days.

The auction ends on November 24.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

Recent findings suggest that my morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Industry observers note that over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

In a recent development, one night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

Could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

According to recent reports, over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

Fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

Sources indicate that health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

Sources indicate that L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

Still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” said Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

In a recent development, “Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian mentioned. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

Recent findings suggest that no more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Industry observers note that even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

In a recent development, I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

You can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

“Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he remarked. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

Recent findings suggest that so, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

  • It has been revealed that for those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, physical buttons have a lot going for them. They’re easy to find by feel, satisfying to use, and generally pretty good at staying wherever the automaker installed them. Well, it seems Audi has an idea that would change that last part: it involves hiding the buttons behind a touchscreen, then deploying them when needed.

In a recent development, as CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed for a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge. The screen stays fixed, while the physical controls swing into position beneath it. Interestingly, when stowed, the bar apparently has an on-screen counterpart with the same functions lined up in the same order, so those who don't want physical buttons can avoid them entirely.

It has been revealed that for those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited. First, Audi says in its patent documents with the German government that the switches can deploy at startup, via voice controls, or via gestures. Moving the controls from the screen to the physical switches also provides more total screen room for users. (In one example, the physical bar deploys when a movie opens, leaving more room for the video.).

Ultimately, this could be a great way to meet the demands of more people. Designers love a clean dashboard without physical buttons and switches. Plenty of drivers really love having that switchgear. This system allows owners to pick whatever they want on the fly.

The timing makes plenty of sense too. Audi has openly said that it views moving toward more mechanical controls as the right direction. Of course, adding extra complexity to the once-simple idea of buttons also can increase the cost down the line when it comes time for repairs, but even so, this idea is certainly a fascinating solution to a very modern problem.

The Failure Rate of Public Schools Is a Tragedy

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.

In a recent development, as described in the article “In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own?,” teenager Najya Hannah-Jones confronted her mother, the prominent journalist Nikole Hannah-Jones, about the choice to send her to public school in a system that, for many, provides substandard education. It was refreshing to read of Najya fighting to get a better education, a striking contrast with the popular but often inaccurate stereotype of lazy teens aiming to learn as little as possible. More importantly, kudos to Nikole Hannah-Jones for candidly admitting in her article that teachers lied to her about what they were teaching and, worse, tried to deceive both mother and daughter about what had actually been learned.

Industry observers note that every parent has a duty to nurture their children, but all parents also must consider their values when choosing schools for their children, so it is heartbreaking to realize that Ms. Hannah-Jones could have chosen a far better public school in Upcoming York for her daughter that would have met the core values listed in her article. Public school? Check. Racially diverse or perhaps even predominately Black student body? Check. Most importantly, a track record of meeting educational standards and being honest with parents regarding what their child is learning and how they are performing? Check and check.

According to recent reports, the truth is that Nikole Hannah-Jones could have enrolled her daughter in a local public school where the majority of students are Black and other nonwhite families and has long offered much better odds for positive educational outcomes. There has long been such an option available to parents that is too often ignored: New York City charter schools.

In the book Charter Schools and Their Enemies, Thomas Sowell painstakingly and convincingly indicates that public charter schools in Newly introduced York City consistently outperform neighborhood schools. Based on Ms. Hannah-Jones essay, one could argue that is not an especially high bar, but the data in the book show academic superiority relative to even the higher-quality schools in New York City, New York State, and nationwide. It is noteworthy that Sowell meticulously controls for the usual “straw men” used to assault charter schools. Indeed, some of the charter schools were not only in the same neighborhoods, but in the same building as the comparison schools in his study.

It has been revealed that it is an ongoing tragedy that Ms. Hannah-Jones and others in the Black community are not demanding an expansion of public charter school options for their children. After all, and perhaps this is why they are under assault, public charter schools provide prima facia evidence that New York can, in fact, deliver a high-quality public education, but chooses not to do so. One hopes that other families like the Hannah-Joneses will enroll their children in public charter schools and demand that New York City be more honest what is being taught and what their children have learned.

The national discussion Ms. Hannah-Jones has sparked has been overwhelmingly focused on schools with majority Black student enrollment, but the debate should not be narrowly circumscribed. The truth is that every teen enrolled in failing schools across the U.S. should be asking their parents the same question Najya Hannah-Jones asked her mother: Why are you sending me to a school you already know is delivering a substandard education?

It has been revealed that stripped to essentials, Ms. Hannah-Jones faced the same choice most families do when deciding whether to enroll their children in public schools, regardless of race: If I send my child to the local school as a kindergartner, what is the probability that my child will emerge from 8th grade with the basic reading and math skills needed to succeed in high school and beyond? It turns out that there are ample data to help parents answer this question.

According to recent reports, the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) provides annual statistics on U.S. education outcomes. Nationally, only 26% of 8th-graders are proficient or above in math, according to its 2022 Nation's Report Card; only about one in four children are entering high school with grade-level proficiency in math. Reading outcomes are only slightly better, with 28% of 8th-graders being rated as proficient. Candidly, this is a national disgrace that poses an excruciating dilemma for parents and students.

A usual response to this data is to argue that public schools are underfunded. New York spends an average of more than $30,000 per student. Overall, the U.S. consistently spends more per pupil than nearly every other country in the world, including many that deliver better outcomes while paying less than half of what the U.S spends. More money is not translating to better outcomes. Does anyone believe that even doubling expenditures or even tripling them would appreciably improve outcomes at the school Najya Hannah-Jones attended, or any other failing school? After all, real spending, even adjusted for inflation, has more than doubled in the past 25 years and outcomes are actually a bit worse nationwide over the same period.

It has been revealed that if it is not simply spending more money, what should parents do? The best answer: Do your homework. There are often options. Many states have adopted public options, including public charter schools, public magnet schools, and other similar approaches.

In a recent development, several of my own children attended a public school implementing a Montessori teaching approach and two of my granddaughters are currently enrolled in a similar public school in Nashville. I was (and am) very pleased with what they were taught, how they were taught, and what they learned. Another daughter attended an academic magnet public high school that consistently outperforms even the most expensive private schools, even though, in general, Nashville public schools often have relatively poor outcomes for most students. The evidence is overwhelming that public school systems know how to deliver a high-quality education. Why are they choosing not to? Najya Hannah-Jones is absolutely right to demand answers and all teens—and their parents—should be asking the same questions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • East Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots.
  • Industry observers note that each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jingle-playing, googly-eyed team of trash-collecting robots are vying to make the world’s busiest rail station a bit cleaner.

East Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots. The machines stand just over three feet tall, and roll autonomously along preprogrammed routes through the station’s underground concourses between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. Once full, they trundle back to the station’s garbage collection area on their own.

Industry observers note that each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line. They definitely don’t look like your average sad, overflowing waste bin. Instead, they stroll up to commuters with bright lights and a front-facing screen showing cartoon eyes. Music appears to play when trash gets fed into them. An accompanying illustration of  Shinjukuma, the station’s bear mascot, shows passengers which bins are for general trash and which are for plastic bottles. It’s all very Japanese.

JR East officials are hoping these bins on wheels will help relieve some of the burden on garbage collectors who struggle to keep up with trash generated by the millions  of people  passing through every day. The station, which sits on the western edge of central Tokyo, sees nearly three million daily passengers, an absurd amount of foot traffic that earned it a Guinness World Record. But more people means more trash. According to Tokyo Weekender, sanitation workers in the station unload garbage from fixed bags more than 10 times per day.

In a recent development, the robots could help, but only if they don’t get in the way and create more problems than they solve. Though JR East reportedly tested out a pair of garbage robots back in 2023, that was in a much smaller station and only for three days. Shinjuku is a much bigger challenge and serves as a kind of stress test to see if they are able to operate safely and effectively in densely packed areas.

Tokyo isn’t the only city experimenting with trash robots. A cat-themed, mobile trash unit made a brief appearance in Paris’ Charles De Gaulle airport last year. In Singapore, an autonomous robot started collecting garbage in 2019 at Jewel Changi Airport, the shopping complex attached to the city’s main airport. And while trash collection is still relatively niche, automated cleaning robots are quickly becoming mainstays in many modern transportation hubs. Houston, Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and Oakland are among the many  cities in the United States already putting robot cleaners to work scrubbing and mopping airport floors.

According to recent reports, making these robots seem cute isn’t just for attracting selfies. It’s also a self-defense strategy. Humans have a mixed track record when it comes to sharing space with robots. In 2024, the Latest York Police Department retired a 400-pound, egg-shaped surveillance robot from patrolling subway lines after facing pushback from privacy activists and concerned citizens, some of whom felt uncomfortable near the lifeless, imposing monitor. Years earlier, a friendly hitchhiking robot called HitchBot made it about two weeks into its trip across the United States when it was found vandalized and beheaded in Philadelphia.

Recent findings suggest that could cartoon eyes and a cute mascot have saved those robots? It’s difficult to say, but at least the Tokyo garbage robots seemed to make it through their trial without any dissected parts. That’s an improvement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With declining sales, annual capacity cuts approaching a million units, and a wave of affordable Chinese competitors entering Western markets, Volkswagen is facing down its own mortality. Rather than fighting it, the company is leaning in and announcing plans to export roughly 300,000 Made-in-China VWs per year by 2030.

In a recent development, american dealers won’t be getting any Made-in-China vehicles (not at first, anyway), but for Mexican, South American, Middle Eastern, African, and Southeast Asian markets, the shift to lower-cost Chinese manufacturing marks a major strategic pivot. In addition to exporting budget-friendly sedans like the Jetta VA3, Volkswagen is also considering a move to adopt Xpeng’s tech stack for up to 75% of its core European lineup.

According to recent reports, the move comes as Volkswagen’s Chinese JVs face a sharp sales decline in their home market, selling just 1.2 million new cars in the first nine months of 2026 (down 35% compared to last year). The financial story is even worse, with last year’s roughly $815 million profit falling to a more than $120 million loss.

“The sharp decline in the overall market in China remains an industry-wide challenge,” remarked Martin Sander, Volkswagen Group’s sales boss, before adding that VW’s “newly introduced, locally developed electric models are beginning to make an impact.”.

Add in rising energy costs, continuing software issues, and serious labor disputes with the IG Metall union in Europe, and Volkswagen may not have much choice in the matter – which is why it’s not exactly surprising to see VW consider turning China into an export hub. And that 300,000 number? That may be just the start.

On Volkswagen’s third-quarter results call, CFO Arno Antlitz reportedly called that 300,000 annual export target “conservative,” adding that overseas shipments could help offset the carmaker’s weakening prospects in China.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the past two decades, if you were looking for an upscale three-row German SUV, the Audi Q7 or its performance-oriented SQ7 sibling was likely on your shopping list. Both have long delivered on style, family-friendliness, and luxury.

According to recent reports, the mid-size Audi SUVs are completely newly introduced for 2027, but the automaker has been careful not to stray too far from a blueprint that has proved so successful. With this latest generation, the Q7’s design has been brought up to speed with the rest of the Audi lineup. That means softer edges, a more muscular stance, and a lot more digital displays inside.

While the Q7’s dimensions grow slightly in most directions, it’s still roughly the same size as before, and its three-row layout could best be described as a 5+2, as the cramped rearmost chairs are best used by children and only in a pinch. If you need more space, there’s now a full-size Q9 model that’s larger inside and out.

See all results for latest 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 29405.

Sources indicate that the Q7 does gain a sought-after second-row feature: optional captain’s chairs. Choosing the two-seat second row reduces seat count from seven to six, but it also decreases the risk of sibling quarrels.

It has been revealed that speaking of the cabin, we’ve complained that Audi’s latest interiors haven’t lived up to the standard set by the company’s earlier efforts, but the newly introduced Q7 represents a reversal of that trend. Granted, the models we sampled were well-optioned examples, but the interior materials are premium, and even the $72,295 base model gets genuine leather upholstery and real wood inlays.

Upgrade to a higher Q7 trim, and you’ll enjoy luxuries such as soft-close doors, a Bang & Olufsen stereo, and massaging front seats. The SQ7 comes in just one trim level, starting at $100,095, and it’s comprehensively equipped with only a few available packages, most of them designed to improve performance and handling.

Industry observers note that special attention has been paid to the SUV’s exterior lighting elements. There are a lot of them, and some are genuinely useful, none more so than Audi’s digital matrix headlights.

Not only do these high-tech headlamps deliver a shockingly bright view of the road ahead, but they also sense oncoming vehicles and will temporarily deactivate some of their bulbs to avoid blinding other motorists. A set of OLED taillights illuminate in different ways depending on context, with the intent to help communicate with other drivers: For example, if another vehicle is too close to the Q7’s rear bumper in traffic, the lights will illuminate with additional brightness as a warning to back off.

In a recent development, other flashy features push into gimmick territory. There’s a light-up grille, a customizable taillamp and daytime-running-light signature, and a system that projects arrows on the street surface to indicate which direction the driver is signaling. Are blinkers no longer enough? Luckily, if you don’t want your Audi lighting up like a Christmas tree, some of these features can be deactivated via the Q7’s infotainment system.

See all results for new 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 29405.

Speaking of infotainment, there are a lot of screens inside the Q7. A large infotainment touchscreen is expected, surely, but there’s also a digital gauge display, a passenger’s display, and an optional head-up display.

While the previous-generation Q7 offered a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four as standard with a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 as an upgrade, the 2027 model ditches the four-banger altogether, making a V-6 standard. This version’s six—a turbo 2.9-liter—packs 429 horsepower, a 94-hp advantage over the outgoing model.

Recent findings suggest that A twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 has always powered the SQ7, and the new generation is no different. It also gets more power, jumping from 500 horsepower in 2026 to 591 horsepower in 2027.

Acceleration is plentiful in the Q7, which makes quick work of highway passing maneuvers and will beat most regular traffic off the line with a quick stab of the throttle. Audi estimates a 4.8-second 60-mph time.

The SQ7 is another animal altogether. While both SUVs have launch control, using it in the SQ7 results in a giggle-inducing run to highway speeds. Audi wagers a 60-mph run would take just 3.7 seconds. The V-8’s muted burble is a bonus.

Confident and predictable handling, an Audi touchstone, remains the default. While all Q7s come with Balanced, Dynamic, and Comfort drive modes, those with the optional air-spring suspension benefit most, with each mode delivering noticeably different ride qualities. SQ7s get air springs as standard but can be optioned with a sport-tuned version of the system, which lowers the ride height 1.2 inches in Dynamic mode and firms everything up to the max.

SQ7 models also feature a retuned all-wheel-drive system with more rear bias. Unlike previous Audi performance SUVs, which were short on driving drama, the new SQ7’s more fun-loving nature shines on twisty roads with that newfound rear-end boogie. Our test drive took us down some of northern California’s twistiest roads, and both SUVs proved entertaining and luxurious.

With this newly introduced generation, Audi has boosted the Q7 and SQ7’s swank factor. It has modernized their styling without introducing a new polarizing design language while adding options buyers want. Retaining the Q7’s just-right size and keeping the focus on refined, performance-oriented road manners is the hedge that will keep it near the top of the shopping list of enthusiast drivers who need family-sized space.

Latest Update: Every Choice Is a Loss: Why We Often Regret Lives Not Lived

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • It has been revealed that nurses often recount stories of patients near the end of their lives who express regrets about experiences they never had and paths they never took.
  • Industry observers note that in the first part of Either/Or, Søren Kierkegaard—writing through the persona of a young man, "A"—posits that life is inherently characterized by boredom and that the choices we make are attempts to escape this state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

It has been revealed that nurses often recount stories of patients near the end of their lives who express regrets about experiences they never had and paths they never took. They sometimes wonder whether choosing differently might have made them more satisfied with their lives. Regret is, to some extent, part of almost everyone's life. If we marry, we may eventually regret it; if we do not, we may remain alone and regret that too. If we emigrate, we may regret leaving; if we stay and endure our circumstances, we may regret that as well. Whether we remain in a tedious job or choose another, whether we speak our minds to those around us or keep silent, we may still end up regretting our choices.

Industry observers note that in the first part of Either/Or, Søren Kierkegaard—writing through the persona of a young man, "A"—posits that life is inherently characterized by boredom and that the choices we make are attempts to escape this state. We choose things that promise pleasure, yet such choices never lead to lasting joy or satisfaction; what is thrilling today may become mundane and tedious by tomorrow. Boredom inevitably returns, leaving us to lament the choices we made and wish we had chosen differently. To break this cycle of regret and boredom, "A" offers an intriguing proposal: much like farmers who rotate crops to prevent soil erosion, individuals should constantly alter their approach to life—avoiding fixation on any single experience—in order to mitigate boredom. Praising the character of Don Juan—the seductive, womanizing figure from Mozart’s opera—"A" champions the rejection of all commitments as a means to banish boredom and regret. In the same volume, Kierkegaard introduces another character, Johannes, who employs psychological tactics to seduce a young woman named Cordelia, gradually cultivating her affection. He uses strategies such as maintaining distance, employing silence, sowing doubt, and stirring the other person’s emotions—all of which he finds deeply pleasurable.

In the second part, Kierkegaard writes through another persona, Judge Wilhelm. He recommends that “A” choose an ethical and committed life. A significant portion of this section addresses marriage. Wilhelm argues that only a stable, committed relationship can prevent the initial fire of love and passion from swiftly burning out, allowing it instead to endure. Through Wilhelm's voice, Kierkegaard writes that our choices shape our ultimate selves—an idea later further developed within existentialist philosophy. By employing pseudonymous characters, Kierkegaard deliberately avoids taking sides, leaving the conclusion to the reader. Ultimately, he presents choice and regret as fundamental components of human existence [1].

Now, we explore the neurological mechanisms underlying the persistent human experience of regret. In their book The Molecule of More, Lieberman and Long discuss two brain circuits—the mesolimbic and the mesocortical—both of which utilize dopamine as a neurotransmitter. The first circuit primarily drives "wanting," motivation, and the anticipation of a reward; it is not about the pleasure itself but rather the anticipated pleasure expected from a given stimulus. The second circuit activates top-down pathways for impulse control, enabling consideration of the future consequences of one's decisions and desires. From an evolutionary perspective, this capacity has allowed humans to transcend immediate, relatively simple responses and blueprint for the attainment of long-term goals. However, this simplified model of the reward system’s neurology suggests that repetition of a stimulus leads to a diminished reward—driven by a decline in dopamine levels and function within the mesolimbic system—thereby shifting attention and motivation toward new rewards [2].

Although the prefrontal cortex is primarily responsible for logical reasoning, evaluation, and behavioral regulation, certain regions within it also play a role in generating feelings of regret. A 2004 study revealed that individuals with damage to the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), unlike healthy controls, did not report experiencing regret or anticipating negative outcomes during a gambling task. Additionally, other brain areas, such as the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the hippocampus, contribute to the experience of regret by enabling the mental simulation of alternative, unlived scenarios [3].

In an intriguing paper published in Science Advances in 2023, researchers examined the distinct roles of the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), the ventral striatum, and dopaminergic neurons in counterfactual thinking in monkeys. Their findings indicated that the brain can represent not only the reward actually received but also the value of a reward that could have been obtained through a different choice [4]. This suggests that, at times, the source of our regret is not an event that actually occurred in real life, but rather an event that never took place, yet one whose possibility the mind has retained. In effect, we may find ourselves mourning a life we ​​never lived.

In conclusion, the human brain is designed to anticipate the future outcomes of decisions we might have made and to compare those potential results with our current situation. While this capacity can aid in making better future choices, it can also foster a chronic sense of regret. This trait leads us to constantly evaluate our present circumstances against hypothetical alternatives—lamenting the paths we did not take. In the modern era, this inclination has been exacerbated by the rise of social media, which offers numerous opportunities for social comparison and exposes us to constant reminders of "alternative" lives. Observing the lives, homes, cities, and joys of others can trigger anxiety that we are perpetually falling behind.

In a recent development, here, it helps to distinguish this phenomenon into two types: 1) Constructive Regret, which helps us recognize past mistakes and make better decisions moving forward; and 2) Ruminative Regret, which traps individuals in a cycle of constantly comparing their actual lives with hypothetical scenarios or the lives of others—without necessarily leading to any constructive action or decision. Since it is impossible to experience every life possibility or to know for certain whether a different choice would have been better, we can take the message of the second part of Either/Or to heart: By committing fully to our own lives, rather than constantly dwelling on lost possibilities, we can liberate ourselves from the anxiety and the wearying melancholy of regret.

In a recent development, 2. Lieberman, D. Z. and M. E. Long (2018). The Molecule of More: How a Single Chemical in Your Brain Drives Love, Sex, and Creativity--and Will Determine the Fate of the Human Race, BenBella Books.

3. Camille N, Coricelli G, Sallet J, Pradat-Diehl P, Duhamel JR, Sirigu A. The involvement of the orbitofrontal cortex in the experience of regret. Science. 2004 May 21;304(5674):1167-70.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.

In fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years.

Sources indicate that although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an crucial concern. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people in the United States experience foodborne illness each year.

However, there are simple steps you can take to reduce the risk of foodborne illness when preparing holiday meals and storing leftovers.

While there were several food recalls in the United States over the summer, two of the largest involved Salmonella linked to jalapeños and Cyclospora linked to lettuce.

These outbreaks prompted widespread recalls and raised concerns about the safety of certain foods, particularly fresh produce.

Although health officials have since declared the major outbreaks over, some consumers may still be hesitant to purchase foods associated with previous recalls.

Even with this declaration, you may still feel nervous about purchasing certain foods, but experts say you don’t need to worry.

“Here in the United States, we have the safest food supply in the world. The recent recalls show that our food safety system is working,” remarked William Schaffner, MD, Professor, Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University.

Sources indicate that michelle Routhenstein, preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, told Healthline that past recalls do not mean entire food categories need to be avoided. The important thing is whether the specific product you have matches a current recall, based on details such as brand, lot number, package size, and expiration date.

“You should enjoy familiar foods, including properly cooked poultry, washed fruits and vegetables, and pasteurized dairy products,” she said. “The key is checking relevant recalls and practicing safe food handling.”.

“Before shopping or cooking, review FDA and USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) recall information and compare any relevant notices with the labels on your ingredients,” said Routhenstein.

Check the pantry and freezer, too: something purchased months ago may still be affected.

“Stay alert to any news reports about food recalls and use good food preparation practices. Those simple actions should keep your holidays happy and safe,” said Schaffner.

Schaffner emphasized the importance of following safe food-handling practices when preparing everyday meals and holiday gatherings.

Recent findings suggest that “Remember the longstanding advice: keep food hot or cold. Avoid long times at room temperature,” he remarked.

Routhenstein advised focusing on four basics: clean, separate, cook, and chill.

Schaffner noted the importance of refrigerating leftovers promptly rather than leaving them at room temperature for extended periods. He recommends clearing the table and refrigerating leftovers soon after the meal ends.

Routhenstein reiterated that you should refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours rather than leaving them out to cool.

Divide turkey into smaller portions and transfer sides and gravy into shallow containers to help them cool swiftly, she advised.

Leftovers can typically be stored in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. If you don’t plan to eat them within that time, consider freezing them.

The important thing is to keep an eye out for any newly introduced recalls, practice food safety, and enjoy your holiday meals!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BMW’s new iX4 is almost here, and it could make range anxiety a thing of the past. With 428 miles of EPA range, more than 500 miles on the WLTP cycle, and ultra-fast charging, the new EV could make road trips a whole lot easier.

Series production of the upcoming iX4 is officially underway at BMW Group’s manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary.

The iX4 is the second fully electric BMW model built at the facility, following the record-breaking production ramp-up of the fresh iX3 SUV.

BMW stated the plant began series production of an entirely latest model in less than two months after the tech giant introduced a 24-hour, three-shift schedule to ramp up output to meet higher-than-expected demand.

The upcoming iX4 will go on sale in March 2027 as an all-electric replacement for the X4. It will be available in two variants: the BMW iX4 50 xDrive and BMW iX4 40 xDrive, with a range-topping M60 xDrive set to follow shortly after.

Both versions use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The iX4 50 xDrive provides a combined 468 hp and 475 lb-ft of torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds.

The performance M60 version delivers a combined 603 hp and 645 lb-ft of torque, which BMW says is good for a 0 to 60 mph sprint in just 3.9 seconds.

In a recent development, the iX4 features a distinct coupe-SUV-like silhouette rather than the traditional boxy, upright SUV design of the iX3. With a rakish roofline and an aerodynamic design, the newly introduced iX4 has a drag coefficient of just 0.23.

Like the iX3, the iX4 is based on BMW’s Neue Klasse architecture with its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system.

Recent findings suggest that while EPA figures have yet to be finalized, BMW remarked the upcoming iX4 has an estimated driving range of up to 428 miles on a single charge using a 112.2 kWh battery. Under WLTP conditions, it offers an all-electric range of up to 514 miles (828 km).

Recent findings suggest that thanks to its 800V architecture, BMW’s new iX4 can add up to 184 miles of range (384 km on the WLTP cycle) in just 10 minutes with charging speeds of up to 400 kW. Charging the vehicle from 10% to 80% takes about 21 minutes.

Like BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, the latest iX4 features its updated interior design. The setup includes a large 17.9″ infotainment screen and BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a 42″ display spanning the base of the windshield.

It has been revealed that would Electrek consider adding a small “Markets” box at the top of each article, with checkmarks next to the regions the news applies to (North America, Europe, China, etc.)? It would make it easy to see at a glance whether a vehicle or announcement applies to your market without having to dig through the article for a mention in the last paragraph.

The iX4 is 188.3″ long, 74.6″ wide, and 63.3″ tall, with a 114.1″ wheelbase, which is about the same size as the iX3. However, it’s slightly lower than the iX3 thanks to the sloped roofline.

Like all Gen6 BMW models, the new iX4 supports bidirectional charging, enabling it to be used as a mobile power source for e-bikes, camping equipment, or other electrical devices.

According to recent reports, the latest BMW iX4 50 xDrive will go on sale in March 2027, starting at $66,300, or $4,800 more than the iX3 50 xDrive. That doesn’t include the $1,495 destination fee.

In Germany, the upcoming BMW iX4 40 xDrive starts at €70,900 ($77,500), and in the UK it’s priced from £53,250 ($69,500), OTR.
