💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX are working toward a year-end deadline to agree on their all-stock merger, according to the Financial Times.
  • Industry observers note that the FT also named the directors negotiating for each side.
  • It has been revealed that we’ve been tracking the Tesla-SpaceX merger since Musk first floated it in May, when we called it Musk’s fourth billion-dollar self-deal, and his first trillion-dollar self-deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX are working toward a year-end deadline to agree on their all-stock merger, according to the Financial Times. A signed deal by December 31 would land days before the upcoming Congress, where Democrats have promised to dig into Musk’s companies, is sworn in on January 3.

Industry observers note that the FT also named the directors negotiating for each side. Two of Tesla’s three are the same people who designed Musk’s $1 trillion pay package.

It has been revealed that we’ve been tracking the Tesla-SpaceX merger since Musk first floated it in May, when we called it Musk’s fourth billion-dollar self-deal, and his first trillion-dollar self-deal. Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX could announce the deal as soon as December. The FT report adds a deadline, names and a vote threshold.

According to the FT, the talks are “moving towards a potential year-end deadline,” even though people familiar with the negotiations say an agreement isn’t close. The combined group would be worth about $3.5 trillion, by far the largest merger ever.

Sources indicate that so why year-end? Look at the calendar.

In a recent development, the new Congress is seated on January 3. As of November 24, AP’s count has Democrats at 258 House seats and 56 Senate seats. Democrats haven’t been subtle about what comes next: Sen. Ruben Gallego tagged Musk on X with “See you in January,” and SpaceX’s military contracts and Musk’s Starlink decisions over Ukraine are expected to be early investigation targets.

Sources indicate that it’s not only Washington. Texas’ incoming attorney general told Bloomberg that a merger of this size “warrants tremendous scrutiny,” and Bloomberg had previously reported that the companies want to close before President Trump leaves office.

Tesla’s special committee is chair Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung, advised by Evercore. SpaceX is represented by Roelof Botha and Randy Glein, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as advisers. Both banks also helped take SpaceX public in June.

Industry observers note that denholm and Wilson-Thompson should sound familiar. They were the two-person special committee that built Musk’s new CEO pay package after a Delaware judge voided his 2018 award. And that 2025 award has change-in-control terms that drop its operational milestones and vest earned shares at the deal price, so the committee that wrote it is now negotiating the deal that could trigger it.

Ira Ehrenpreis, a long-time friend of Musk, who chairs Tesla’s compensation and governance committees and has sat on SpaceX’s board since February, isn’t on Tesla’s committee, per the FT.

In a recent development, if you can believe it, Musk isn’t formally in the room. The FT notes Texas governance rules keep him out of active negotiations, but both committees can consult senior executives for information. Every one of those executives reports to Musk.

It has been revealed that any agreement goes to a separate extraordinary Tesla shareholder meeting, and it needs more than 50% of all outstanding votes, not just of votes cast. Abstentions and uncast shares effectively count as “no.”.

That sounds like a high bar. But Musk holds about 20% of Tesla’s voting power, and nothing in the report says his shares will be excluded. If they count, he’s 40% of the way to approval before a single other shareholder votes. On the other side, Musk controls about 84% of SpaceX’s votes, so there’s no real suspense there.

Uncast retail votes are exactly what Tesla’s new auto-vote program, rolled out in its October proxy, was designed to reduce.

Then there’s the regulatory side. The FT states the deal could draw scrutiny in the US, China, Europe and the UK, with Tesla’s China operations sitting awkwardly next to SpaceX’s rocket and Starlink business, which does a lot of work for the US military. Giga Shanghai builds more than half of Tesla’s cars.

Congress can’t block this merger. Antitrust review sits with Trump’s DOJ and FTC until 2029, plus China, the EU and the UK.

According to recent reports, it's probably already too late to escape Jan 3. The DoJ investigation into the merger will take a minimum of a few months. At the very least it looks like there is a 30 mandatory waiting period, so if the merger isn't announced by Dec 4, that 30 days takes them to Jan 3. That gives them 10 calendar days to finish negotiations and get stock holder approval and they have to give time for the voters to get their votes in. So short of some miracle, Musk isn't going to get this done before Jan 3 ... at least from my understanding and counting.

Sources indicate that what congressional committees can do is subpoena. Committee minutes, the Evercore fairness work, emails between Denholm’s committee and Musk’s executives about how the exchange ratio got set. That’s the kind of record that got Musk’s 2018 pay package voided by a Delaware judge, and it’s the kind of record nobody wants dragged into a hearing mid-negotiation.

Industry observers note that the talks are “not close,” yet there’s a deadline. When the deadline comes from the political calendar instead of the negotiation, the side that wants to close fast is the one giving ground. But in this case, Musk is both sides, but he is mainly SpaceX.

It has been revealed that we’ve stated it before, and we’ll keep saying it: the only vote that means anything here is a majority of Tesla shareholders not named Musk. Denholm, who is up for re-election at next week’s December 3 annual meeting, could commit to that today, but in her entire tenure as Tesla chair, she always did exactly what Musk wanted.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in a break from tradition, the park rangers at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska have awarded one of their 2026 Anan Bear Awards to a completely different animal species. For its tenacity in finding food, a small mink (Neogale vison)  walking around Anan Creek wins the On a Mission Award.

According to recent reports, “This little mink was a frequent visitor at the trailhead and the beach in Anan,” the rangers write. “It seemed unconcerned by nearby humans, completely focused on the small crabs and other nibbles it could get ahold of. It was on a mission to eat!”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears (and a lucky mink) spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Recent findings suggest that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States and covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish and survive the long winter ahead. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own antics and quirks.

In addition to the bears and mink, numerous other animals call Tongass home. Bald eagles (Haliaeetus leucocephalus), the Alexander Archipelago wolf (Canis lupus ligoni), and the Sitka black-tailed deer (Odocoileus hemionus sitkensis). Importantly, all five of North America’s Pacific salmon species are found within the forest—Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), coho (Oncorhynchus kisutch), pink (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha), sockeye  (Oncorhynchus nerka), and chum (Oncorhynchus keta). These five fish species help feed the bears and other mammals and birds who gather here.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s no secret that electric cars are more affordable to maintain than their gasoline-powered counterparts. While they may have a higher purchase price than a comparable gas-powered vehicle, EVs can save owners money over time by eliminating the need for regular engine oil changes, emissions tests, and other traditional maintenance tasks. Affordable electric vehicles are also becoming increasingly common, with even more options expected to arrive in the coming years.

Sources indicate that however, that doesn't mean electric cars are completely maintenance-free. Like any other vehicle, EVs require regular care and attention to remain reliable and perform at their best for many years.

Although they don't have conventional combustion engines or traditional automatic transmissions, electric cars still feature components that require periodic maintenance. These include reduction gearboxes, brake fluid, brake pads, coolant systems, and tires among other things. Keeping these components in good condition is essential to ensuring an EV's long-term reliability.

For the second installment of our EV maintenance series, I'll be taking a closer look at the Hyundai Ioniq 5, one of the most recognizable electric crossovers on the market. Made in the United States and South Korea, the Ioniq 5 has long been one of the biggest rivals to the ubiquitous Tesla Model Y.

I'll break down Hyundai's recommended maintenance schedule, explaining which items are required to keep the vehicle running smoothly over the long term.

Compared to Tesla, which is known for its rather skimpy maintenance plan, Hyundai includes a generous list of maintenance items in the owner’s manual. The automaker also includes additional service actions that should be performed if the car is used in harsher-than-normal conditions, so owners know what to expect in the long run.

It has been revealed that there’s a normal maintenance schedule and a separate section for severe usage and low mileage conditions. Hyundai also has a list of maintenance items that can be performed by the owner. I’ll go through all of them, so drivers can easily mark down what needs to be done during the car’s lifetime.

In a recent development, hyundai notes that normal driving conditions include distances longer than 10 miles, clean roads without salt or dust, ambient temperatures under 90ºF (32ºC), no towing, no roof rack, and normal speeds. Under these conditions, the required maintenance for a Hyundai Ioniq 5 is as follows, according to the owner’s manual:.

According to Hyundai, extra precaution needs to be taken if the car is driven under certain conditions. These include repeated driving short distances of less than five miles in normal temperatures or less than 10 miles in freezing temperatures, and driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, graveled, or salt-spread roads.

In a recent development, but that’s not all. Driving in areas using salt or other corrosive materials, or in very cold weather, driving in heavy dust conditions, driving in heavy traffic areas with the ambient temperature higher than 90ºF (32 ºC) while consuming more than 50% of electric energy, and driving on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads repeatedly can also result in extra maintenance items.

Towing a trailer, using a roof rack, driving as a patrol car or taxi, frequently driving at high speeds, and frequently driving in stop-and-go conditions are also part of the conditions that lead to more intense servicing requirements.

In addition to the normal maintenance schedule above, Hyundai recommends the following actions for severe usage and low-mileage conditions:.

All of these items should be performed by a Hyundai technician, but the Ioniq 5 also has a consistent list of maintenance actions that should be performed by the owner.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is one of the best-selling electric crossovers in the United States, and for good reason. Its unique styling has plenty of fans, and it’s a genuinely nice car to drive. As for its maintenance requirements, the official recommendations have a lot more items compared to the Tesla Model Y, but at the end of the day, most of them are just inspection jobs. As a result, maintenance costs should be quite low compared to a comparable gas vehicle. Just rotate and replace tires, keep an eye on your brakes, and swap out the coolant after 10 years or 120,000 miles.

Breaking: Nuro pulls safety drivers from Lucid Gravity Uber robotaxis in Bay Area

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that nuro is now testing Lucid Gravity robotaxis on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with nobody in the driver’s seat.
  • It’s the biggest step yet for the Uber-Nuro-Lucid partnership.
  • According to Nuro’s announcement, driverless testing covers Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos, and Sunnyvale, with more Bay Area cities to follow next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that nuro is now testing Lucid Gravity robotaxis on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with nobody in the driver’s seat. The driverless testing starts in four Peninsula and South Bay cities, with a fleet of more than 100 Gravity SUVs delivered by Lucid for the program.

It’s the biggest step yet for the Uber-Nuro-Lucid partnership. But it comes with a quieter patch: the public launch, originally promised for 2026, is now expected in Q1 2027.

According to Nuro’s announcement, driverless testing covers Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos, and Sunnyvale, with more Bay Area cities to follow next year. Uber employees will “soon” be able to ride in the driverless vehicles.

Nuro has run the Gravity robotaxis around the clock in the Bay Area and Houston since December 2025, but always with a safety driver. Before pulling the driver, the firm says it ran no-vehicle-operator testing at its Las Vegas closed course, covering things like pedestrian encounters and right-of-way violations, plus large-scale simulation.

In a recent development, tilo Schwarz, Nuro’s head of the Nuro Driver, pointed out that driverless operation “isn’t new” for the organization. That’s fair. Nuro has run driverless delivery pods in California since 2020. But this is its first time doing it with a passenger vehicle.

In a recent development, the regulatory pieces were already in place. As we reported in May, the California DMV extended Nuro’s driverless testing permit to the Lucid Gravity, and the CPUC followed with a drivered pilot permit for carrying passengers.

Nuro states it’s one of just six companies allowed to test without a driver on California roads. The DMV’s list, last updated November 5, confirms it: AutoMo, Nuro, Tensor, Waymo, WeRide, and Zoox.

Sources indicate that tesla isn’t one of them. Its “Tesla Robotaxi LLC” entity only holds a permit to test with a driver in California, and it has no deployment permit either.

It has been revealed that waymo, of course, is the benchmark. It already runs a paid, fully driverless service across much of the Bay Area, including the Peninsula and South Bay where Nuro is just now pulling its safety drivers.

When Lucid, Nuro, and Uber announced the program in July 2025, the plan was to launch “later next year” in a major US city. As recently as June, when Uber named Houston as the second market for mid-2027, the Bay Area launch was still slated for this year.

It has been revealed that now it’s Q1 2027. Not a huge slip, but it’s a slip.

Industry observers note that the scale ambition has gone the other way. Uber’s purchase commitment grew from 20,000 vehicles to at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles with the Nuro Driver, starting with the Gravity and later Lucid’s upcoming midsize models. Uber will own and operate the cars with fleet partners, and they’ll only be available through the Uber app.

For context, Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3 2026. At that pace, 35,000 robotaxis would take more than two years of Lucid’s entire output.

Recent findings suggest that this is real progress, and it deserves credit. Nuro got the permits, built a formal safety case, tested at a closed course, and only then took the driver out. That’s how it should be done, and it should be applauded, especially as some companies claim to lead in autonomy while being too chicken to get a permit in California.

In a recent development, but let’s keep it in perspective. Driverless testing in four suburban cities with a 100-car fleet is where Waymo was years ago. Waymo is already doing hundreds of thousands of paid rides a week, including in the same part of the Bay Area. Nuro and Uber aren’t catching up to Waymo in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the bigger question for me is Lucid. The partnership gives Lucid exactly the kind of volume it needs, and 35,000 vehicles is a big number for a company delivering under 4,000 cars a quarter.

If this program is successful, and that’s a massive if, then it could really help Lucid get to its more affordable vehicle.

Can Pirelli’s Cyber Tyre Technology Replace Drive Modes?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout.
  • According to recent reports, that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data.
  • Industry observers note that "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout. The tires use a sensor that looks a lot like a Dexcom G7 to feed temperature, air pressure, acceleration, and identification data to a vehicle's computers.

According to recent reports, that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data. For example, swap your summer tires for squishier winter rubber, and a compatible car could recognize the change and automatically adjust how its electronic controls intervene, leaving you free to imagine a world where maybe we all just drove better.

See all results for used cars for sale near 45040.

Industry observers note that "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani. The sensor, weighing just 13 grams, is bonded to the tire's inner liner beneath the tread using a specially developed adhesive and rubber housing. The process was developed using learnings from Pirelli's Noise Cancelling System, which uses foam inside the tire to absorb sound waves and reduce cabin vibration. The sensor must survive extreme temperatures, constant flexing, and the insane lateral g-forces that tires are susceptible to at over 200 mph. Engineers explained that its battery is designed to outlast the tire and enters a low-power sleep mode during extended storage.

The more inspiring part is what the car does with the information it gathers. As we found in our recent all-weather tire comparison test, summer, winter, and all-season tires perform dramatically differently. Yet a vehicle's electronic controls are generally calibrated around its original equipment, using things like wheel speed sensors that aren’t as close to the road surface as the Cyber Tyre. Instead, it identifies the specific tire installed at each corner, allowing it to use different wheel-slip targets. And with the sensor attached to the inside of the tire, the data informing those systems is closer to the road surface than ever.

We sampled the technology at Las Vegas Motor Speedway in two Mercedes-AMG GT63 S four-doors wearing Cyber Tyre-equipped P Zero MS all-season tires.

The first exercise had us pin the throttle through a corner from 40 mph using three different traction-control calibrations, all on the same P Zero MS all-season tires. The first, intended for ultra-high-performance summer tires, was overly restrictive, cutting power before the tires could deliver much acceleration. The second, calibrated for winter tires, permitted considerably more wheelspin, making the AMG easy to slide. Despite that setting being the most fun (and our favorite), Cyber Tyre delivered a happy medium, allowing more controlled acceleration without either extreme.

See all results for used cars for sale near 45040.

According to recent reports, this is where Cyber Tyre begins to make the case against selectable drive modes. The same car, wearing the same tires, just behaved three different ways without any mechanical changes. It's not going to replace the button that stiffens your dampers or changes your exhaust note, but it could eventually make some traction-related settings redundant.

The second AMG demonstrated ABS braking from 65 mph. With Cyber Tyre integration active, our stopping distance improved by 0.9 meter, or about three feet, according to Pirelli's instrumentation. That's not dramatically different, but still a measurable improvement.

It has been revealed that of course, these demonstrations weren't proof that Cyber Tyre can outperform a conventional system already calibrated for the correct tires. And the technology isn't smart enough to know it's snowing just because the tires are cold. But the distinction is that Cyber Tyre can give the car information about its tires without the driver doing anything. That could be super useful as tires wear, temperatures change, or owners swap between summer and winter sets. Pirelli is also developing tire-wear estimates using its sensor data, which could prove useful for fleet operators managing hundreds of vehicles.

According to recent reports, pirelli and Bosch confirmed their development partnership in 2024, and the technology has already appeared in vehicles from McLaren and Pagani. Pirelli executives say a substantially higher-volume application should be announced in the first half of 2027, with production expected in 2028. So it's possible this tech could arrive in models as common as a Ford pickup.

It has been revealed that pirelli is also investing approximately $1.2 billion to expand its Rome, Georgia, manufacturing facility, where Cyber Tyre-equipped products will be produced alongside conventional tires. By 2033, the manufacturer expects annual production capacity to reach six million tires and plans to add up to 1000 engineering jobs.

They also recently announced that China's state-owned Sinochem, formerly Pirelli's largest shareholder, reduced its ownership to 13.6 percent in November. The Italian government has restricted Sinochem's influence and specifically prohibited sharing Cyber Tyre data with entities connected to the Chinese government. Following those governance changes, Pirelli received U.S. authorization to market the technology here. Not that anyone was worried about a Pagani Utopia Roadster being a boon of classified information.

Sources indicate that cyber Tyre isn't about to take the Ford Bronco's G.O.A.T. modes out back to shoot them. There are plenty of reasons to let drivers decide how their cars behave. But after experiencing three dramatically different calibrations in the same AMG, it's easy to see why some of those decisions might eventually be better left to the car. Just make sure we’re able to fully disable them.

Recent findings suggest that austin Irwin has worked for Car and Driver for over 10 years in various roles. He's steadily worked his way from an entry-level data entry position into driving vehicles for photography and video, and is now reviewing and testing cars. What will he do next? Who knows, but he better be fast.

By 2040, 51% of People Living with HIV Could Be Over 50

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.
  • In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040.
  • The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.

In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040. An estimated 96% of these older adults will live in low- and middle-income countries.

The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.

These challenges include stigma related to both age and HIV, a higher burden of chronic health conditions, taking multiple medications, delayed diagnoses, physical limitations, and increased financial and social vulnerability.

Factors like these “influence HIV risk for older adults in complex and dynamic ways,” according to the report authors.

Several factors have contributed to the growing population of older adults living with HIV, including:.

Many adults over age 50 who are living with HIV acquired the virus during young adulthood in the late 1990s and early 2000s. During that period, some experienced prolonged periods of uncontrolled HIV and exposure to older ART medications with more severe side effects, which may have contributed to long-term inflammation and other health complications.

William Schaffner, MD, professor in the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “That older persons with HIV are on track to outnumber younger persons with HIV infection is a double-barreled success story.”.

It has been revealed that “First, the effective treatment of persons with HIV infection has resulted in the expectation of normal or near-normal lifespans; thus, more older persons living with HIV infection,” he said. “This is a great success; both in creating effective, easy-to-use medicines as well as developing medical care systems that can reach such patients and provide lifetime care.”.

Schaffner remarked the second success has been educating younger people about HIV prevention, helping reduce fresh infections.

In a recent development, older adults also account for a growing proportion of upcoming HIV diagnoses. They are more likely to receive a diagnosis later in the course of infection, which can delay treatment and increase the risk of serious health complications and death.

Mathematical models project that the average age of people living with HIV worldwide will increase from 41 in 2025 to 50 by 2040, largely driven by demographic shifts in low- and middle-income countries.

While the World Health Organization (WHO) does not specify an upper age limit for HIV testing in its published overview, U.S. guidelines focus on specific age groups.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends routine HIV testing for people ages 13 to 64, and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends testing for people ages 15 to 65.

However, these age limits don’t mean older adults shouldn’t be tested for HIV, as both U.S. organizations also recommend testing older adults who may be at risk.

Older adults can still be sexually active and have a chance of acquiring HIV. Certain physical changes that come with age, such as thinning of vaginal tissue, may also increase the risk of HIV infection.

Industry observers note that despite these risks, older adults are often overlooked in HIV prevention campaigns, research, and clinical trials. The report’s authors say more needs to be done to address these gaps.

“Targeted and tailored HIV prevention and screening services for older adults are a pressing global need,” the report authors stated.

Schaffner agreed with this and added, “Increasing the effectiveness of diagnosis and treatment of HIV infection in older adults will increase their expectation of a healthier, longer life.”.

The report recommends several approaches to improving HIV prevention and screening among older adults, including:.

While Schaffner noted that HIV treatment has “advanced spectacularly over the past 20 years,” making it possible for people living with HIV to lead longer, healthier lives, access to these treatments remains a challenge in many parts of the world.

It has been revealed that bentley may not exactly be the first name in off-road performance, but the British luxury brand made its first moves toward that horizon with a surprise concept in January. Now, it looks like that Bentayga X concept might be headed for production in the near future.

In an interview with Automotive News, CEO Frank-Steffen Walliser says that reaction to the Bentayga X was “really surprisingly positive.” When asked directly if the brand was considering building the concept as a production model, Walliser remarked that “yes, we have this on the horizon. Time will tell us when it’s ready.”.

That is not quite a direct confirmation of production prepares, but it is pretty much as close as an executive will get without directly announcing a new model. It’s also great news for buyers hoping to get their hands on a Bentayga with more off-road capability—an option that has never before been available in the organization’s century-long history.

The concept shown in January added over two inches of ride height and nearly five inches of track width to the basic Bentayga Speed, bringing total ground clearance over 12 inches and total wading depth up to 21.6 inches. While we do not know how much of the concept would make its way into a theoretical production Bentayga X, it would be safe to assume that the final product would ride higher and sit wider than a typical Bentley SUV. All-terrain rubber and extra lighting elements, both seen on the concept, could also presumably make their way to the finished product.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD debuted the third-generation Tang, a large, high-tech five-seat flagship electric SUV, starting at under $30,000 in China.
  • The upcoming third-gen Tang is positioned below the Great Tang, or “Da Tang” as it’s called in China, BYD’s larger seven-seat flagship SUV in its Dynasty lineup.
  • It has been revealed that BYD held a launch event for its new flagship five-seat electric SUV on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD debuted the third-generation Tang, a large, high-tech five-seat flagship electric SUV, starting at under $30,000 in China.

The upcoming third-gen Tang is positioned below the Great Tang, or “Da Tang” as it’s called in China, BYD’s larger seven-seat flagship SUV in its Dynasty lineup.

It has been revealed that BYD held a launch event for its new flagship five-seat electric SUV on Tuesday. The third-gen Tang is available in three variants: standard Premium, Laser Premium, and Laser Flagship.

All versions come standard with rear-wheel drive (RWD), but buyers can upgrade the Laser Flagship model with an optional all-wheel-drive (AWD) steer-by-wire package for an extra 20,000 yuan ($3,000).

Prices for the standard Tang Premium start at 187,900 yuan, or about $28,000, significantly lower than its pre-sale price of 225,000 yuan ($34,000).

The Laser Premium and Laser Flagship models start at 207,900 yuan and 219,900 yuan, respectively, also well below the pre-sale price.

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP Batteries. RWD models use a single 402 hp (300kW) electric motor, delivering CLTC ranges of 453 miles (730 km) for the base Premium model and 528 miles (850 km) for the Laser Premium and Laser Flagship versions.

Upgrading to the dual-motor AWD powertrain bumps power to 690 hp (515 kW) and delivers a CLTC range of up to 478 miles (770 km).

The optional AWD steer-by-wire package adds a premium touch with a drive-by-wire digital chassis, reclining driver’s seats, a 35.4″ integrated Star Ring display screen, and intelligent electric all-wheel-drive.

All versions feature BYD’s Flash Charging tech, enabling it to charge from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes for a full recharge (10% to 97%).

Inside, the flagship SUV adopts a five-seat layout and is packed with huge digital screens and premium extras.

The third-gen Tang features two giant screens: a 35.4″ integrated Star Ring display and a 30″ panoramic theater screen.

BYD stated the five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers, claiming the upcoming Tang SUV has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L. It also offers a generous 1,000 mm of legroom for rear passengers.

The flagship electric SUV is equipped with BYD’s latest tech and other features, including its God’s Eye B laser-assisted driving system with DiPilot300 and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

BYD’s God’s Eye B uses a roof-mounted LiDAR to support ADAS features such as city navigation assist, high-speed navigation assist, and all-scenario parking assist.

The third-gen Tang also has BYD’s new high-speed tire blowout stability system, which can keep the vehicle stable and in its lane at up to 112 mph (180 km/h).

Measuring 5,045 mm long, 1,980 mm wide, and 1,760 mm tall, with a 2,950 mm wheelbase, BYD’s latest Tang SUV is about the size of a Tesla Model X or BMW iX.

The third-gen Tang will join the larger Great Tang as BYD expands its flagship SUV lineup. The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it rolled out in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Industry observers note that since it launched, BYD has sold over 10,000 Great Tangs a month for four consecutive months. Will the smaller five-seat Tang draw the same demand? Let us know what you think of it in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tesla is rolling out the 15th iteration of its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software, and the patch comes with some pretty impressive graphics. It’s called Tesla Reality View, and it’s exactly that, using the vehicle’s cameras to record what’s going on around you, then re-create the scene on the central screen accurately.

It has been revealed that the intent is to show a visual representation of what the latest FSD driver assistance is going to do, as represented by onscreen arrows. Turns are represented, and the screen shows what parking spot the vehicle has selected when using auto park.

According to recent reports, it all looks extremely slick, just like the real world rendered into a video game in real time. Tesla says the actual driving assistance has also been greatly improved, with an increased ability to spot and react to potholes, small animals, and road debris. The system also uses fleet learning from the trips other Teslas take on the same route, something Tesla has been doing for several iterations of FSD.

See all results for used Tesla for sale near 34221.

Although Tesla claims that this fresh iteration is 25 times safer in critical interventions, this claim isn’t backed up with provided data such as miles driven; it’s just Tesla’s claim thus far.

Sources indicate that owners’ experiences since the rollout have indicated that V15 appears to be more cautious in certain situations, and in some cases a little overcautious. Posts on Reddit’s Tesla forum report a vehicle aggressively avoiding random items in the road and reacting to a road repair site as if it was a pothole. Other forum users point out that early FSD updates often are a little shaky right at rollout but more polished by the time the release goes out more broadly.

Our own experience with Tesla’s FSD is that it works flawlessly—right up until it doesn’t and the driver needs to take over. Tesla’s own literature notes that drivers are expected to keep their attention on the road. The pretty upcoming graphics look attractive, but if you’re staring at the screen instead of out the windshield, FSD should theoretically automatically disconnect.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

Breaking: ‘Root-to-Tip’ Eating: Are You Missing Out on Fiber by Discarding Scraps?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eating fruit and veggie scraps may boost fiber intake and cut food waste.
  • This study from King’s College London found that peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of fruits and vegetables—parts often discarded—contained significantly more dietary fiber than the commonly eaten portions in 10 of 12 produce types analyzed.
  • In some cases, the fiber content was up to five times higher in these “root-to-tip” components.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eating fruit and veggie scraps may boost fiber intake and cut food waste.

This study from King’s College London found that peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of fruits and vegetables—parts often discarded—contained significantly more dietary fiber than the commonly eaten portions in 10 of 12 produce types analyzed.

In some cases, the fiber content was up to five times higher in these “root-to-tip” components.

Sources indicate that these findings, recently published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, are noteworthy, since around 95% of U.S. adults aren’t getting enough fiber. What’s more, around one-fifth of all food produced globally is wasted every year.

The researchers identified 12 fresh produce items that were deemed suitable for “root-to-tip” inclusion:.

In the laboratory analysis, they measured the dietary fiber content of both the “root-to-tip” components (skins, peels, seeds, stalks) and the parts that people typically eat.

The key findings of the study highlighted that in 10 of the 12 produce types, the “root-to-tip” components contained more fiber than the parts typically consumed.

However, broccoli stalks contained 28.4% less fiber than the florets that people usually eat, meaning individuals are already consuming the most fiber-rich part.

Most participants in focus groups saw the nutritional value of the “root-to-tip” approach as more of a motivator than its sustainability.

However, these findings show that a “root-to-tip” approach to many fruits and vegetables could not only support higher dietary fiber intake but also reduce food waste.

According to recent reports, kristin Kirkpatrick, president of KAK, Consulting, LLC, and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine, mentioned that the takeaway isn’t to eat every peel or seed, but to look for safe, simple ways to get more fiber from the foods you’re already buying. Kirkpatrick wasn’t involved in the study.

Industry observers note that this applies to some of the plants analyzed in this study, but not all produce. For instance, you can only eat a kiwi that’s peeled. This is still a better choice than no kiwi (or a processed-food snack in its place) at all.

Fiber is crucial for promoting health and preventing chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and obesity.

It has been revealed that “Fiber does much more than support regular bowel movements. It helps regulate blood sugar, supports beneficial gut bacteria, and certain types of soluble fiber can help lower LDL cholesterol by increasing bile acid elimination,” noted Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

On average, adults are recommended to get 25–30 grams (or more, depending on age) of fiber daily.

Both nutrition experts told Healthline that people generally aren’t getting enough fiber because of their food options or choices.

“Most likely because individuals are not consuming enough plants, and overconsuming processed and ultra-processed foods which are typically very low in fiber,” said Kirkpatrick. “Simply not eating enough fruits and vegetables or choosing white refined grains over whole grains can be why a person’s diet is lacking fiber.”.

Routhenstein added, “I think it is vital that when we talk about fiber we point out that it doesn’t have to mean completely changing how you eat. I encourage people to incorporate fiber-rich ingredients into familiar, culturally meaningful foods they already enjoy.”.

“Start with small increases with foods you enjoy and build gradually to allow your digestive system to adjust.”.

It is notable to always research any new plant parts before eating them, wash thoroughly, and consult a healthcare professional if you have digestive conditions or concerns.

And remember that not all produce scraps are edible or recommended.

According to recent reports, “Any dietary change will be dependent on personal preference. Some individuals may not enjoy or may not know how to add components of a plant they are not used to,” said Kirkpatrick.

Industry observers note that she noted that, based on the study’s examples, an easier option might be to add more kiwi peels and seeds. “In fact, kiwi skin is probably the most practical fruit peel to highlight for consumers,” she said.

Routhenstein added, “I think there is a knowledge gap that the skins, peels, from the root to the tip are edible and nutritious, so we need to start there.”.

She suggested that one way to start is by eating the skins of apples, pears, and well-scrubbed carrots. Trim and thinly slice broccoli stalks for stir-fries or soups. Sautée beet greens and stems just as you would spinach. Freeze appropriate vegetable trimmings, such as carrot ends and celery leaves, for homemade broth.

“Root-to-tip eating helps reduce food waste by encouraging us to use more of the edible portions of fruits and vegetables rather than discarding them. It also maximizes the nutritional and economic value of the food we purchase while making better use of the water, land, and energy required to produce it,” stated Routhenstein.

“The key is finding simple, enjoyable ways to incorporate these parts into meals we already eat.”.

#109603. Breaking: Could a giant catapult launch someone to space? Short answer: Yes.

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1370 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Could a giant catapult launch someone to space? Short answer: Yes.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for as long as humans have looked at the night sky, we’ve wondered what lies beyond Earth—and dreamed up ways of getting up there.
  • Recent findings suggest that but what if, instead of modern rockets, we went medieval?
  • The answer requires a little imagination, a lot of physics, and a space-launching siege weapon of truly ridiculous proportions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for as long as humans have looked at the night sky, we’ve wondered what lies beyond Earth—and dreamed up ways of getting up there. These days, powerful rockets carrying tons of fuel are the tried-and-true method of escaping the planet’s gravitational pull and reaching space.

Recent findings suggest that but what if, instead of modern rockets, we went medieval? Could a trebuchet or catapult—the massive siege weapons once used to fling stones at castles—launch a person into orbit? And if so, just how substantial would one have to be?

The answer requires a little imagination, a lot of physics, and a space-launching siege weapon of truly ridiculous proportions.

A catapult is essentially a giant lever used to hurl projectiles. Typically, they have a large, spoon-shaped throwing arm that’s wrenched back, creating tension, and then released, flinging an object over a great distance.

In a recent development, A trebuchet is a kind of catapult that uses a counterweight and gravity to launch projectiles. This machine’s long arm rests on a fulcrum, with a sling or cup for the projectile at one end and a heavy counterweight at the other.

When the arm is released, gravity pulls the counterweight downward, sending the opposite end—and its payload—soaring upward and forward.

Trebuchets are typically more powerful than catapults because they can launch heavier payloads over greater distances. So for our purposes, we’ll be focusing on a space trebuchet rather than a space catapult.

Sources indicate that trebuchets have been hurling heavy objects through the air for centuries. The structures are believed to have originated in China as early as the fifth century BC and eventually spread across Eurasia, becoming a formidable force in medieval warfare.

They arrived in Europe during the 12th century and promptly surpassed simple catapults.

Recent findings suggest that today, trebuchets are no longer used as weapons. But they remain popular as teaching tools for demonstrating physics principles—and for the decidedly more wholesome pursuit of seeing how far we can fling pumpkins, cabbages, and other projectiles.

Recent findings suggest that so let’s crunch the numbers: Could a massive trebuchet really blast a human into orbit? Theoretically, yes. Practically, no.

For help answering this question, Popular Science turned to Frankie Zhu, an assistant professor in space robotics at the Colorado School of Mines in Golden, Colorado. Zhu gamely agreed to do some back-of-the-napkin math to put some numbers to this wildly improbable scenario.

“It just reminds me of a classic physics problem you would encounter in undergrad,” she states.

Recent findings suggest that before we can get to the heart of the calculations, Zhu claims, we need to define some initial parameters. First, because the energy required to send a human into orbit depends on both mass and velocity, we need to know our imaginary astronaut’s mass. Zhu recommends 70 kilograms, or about 154 pounds.

Recent findings suggest that next, we need to define where space—and, for our purposes, orbit—begins. The conventional boundary is the Kármán line, an imaginary line 100 kilometers (about 62 miles) above sea level that is widely used to mark the edge of space. It’s the point at which Earth’s atmosphere becomes too thin for conventional aircraft to generate enough lift to stay aloft. “An orbit at 100 kilometers would be the lowest energy orbit possible,” she states.

Industry observers note that to orbit Earth at the Kármán line—and not plummet back to the ground—a person needs to travel at approximately 7.85 kilometers per second, or 17,500 miles per hour, the same speed the International Space Station travels while orbiting Earth. “Any less and the human would fly up and then come back down in a parabolic trajectory,” she states.

It has been revealed that if we assume that the atmosphere doesn’t produce drag on the human as they fly, then the velocity of the person leaving the trebuchet immediately after launch needs to be at least 7.97 kilometers per second, or 17,828 miles per hour. That extra bit of speed accounts for the energy needed to climb from Earth’s surface to the Kármán line.

According to recent reports, to launch a human at that velocity, the trebuchet would need to store a massive amount of potential energy—about 2.22 billion joules, by Zhu’s calculations, similar to about 1,200 pounds of TNT. Zhu notes that she’s assuming 100 percent mechanical efficiency, meaning that none of the trebuchet’s stored energy is lost to friction, air resistance, sound, deformation, or the movement of the machine itself.

Recent findings suggest that from here, we can move on to the design of the trebuchet. Based on Zhu’s math, the trebuchet would need a 5,000-ton counterweight—the equivalent of roughly 950 African bush elephants—which would need to drop at least 45.2 meters, or roughly 148 feet.

To turn the relatively slow movement of the massive counterweight into a hypersonic launch speed, the trebuchet would need an extreme mechanical leverage ratio of 379:1, she says. With these figures in mind, the trebuchet’s long throwing arm—the part with the human at the end of it—would need to be about 17.14 kilometers, or 10.7 miles, long.

“That should give you all the physical parameters of the trebuchet, ignoring some physics and human welfare,” she jokes.

Industry observers note that how exactly would a human fare under these conditions? Fighter jet pilots can survive up to nine Gs using specialized G-suits, physical straining techniques, and intense centrifuge training. But, Zhu says, the “amount of Gs that the trebuchet is going to reach is…definitely past nine Gs. This human is not going to be alive when they make it to orbit.”.

Another hurdle? Building the trebuchet. “To design a structure that can handle that amount of mass—the 5,000-ton counterweight—to support that mass and then to make something that large… that would be a humanity feat and a structural feat,” she notes.

Sources indicate that how much trash is on the moon? About 412,000 pounds.

Why can’t we just launch all of Earth’s garbage into the sun?

What happens to your body when you die in space?

It has been revealed that is turbulence really like Jell-O? Pilots weigh in.

Why do we put seatbacks up for landing? An aviation expert explains.

Sources indicate that A more human-friendly option, she says, might be a railgun, which uses electromagnetic forces to accelerate a projectile along a pair of conductive rails at extremely high speeds. To launch a person into orbit, a railgun would also need to be “really, really long,” she says. But because the human projectile could accelerate over a much greater distance and for a longer period of time, a railgun would theoretically offer a smoother acceleration profile—one that’s more amenable to human survival.

Recent findings suggest that “Whereas [with] a trebuchet, the acceleration is going to be impulsive,” she states. “It’s going to be a huge smack at the very beginning if the structure doesn’t flex, if the structure is rigid.”.

Industry observers note that rockets have been the standard for launching things into space since 1944, when Germany’s V-2 became the first human-made object to cross the Kármán line. But that doesn’t necessarily mean they’re the most efficient way to get there.

Rockets require enormous amounts of fuel, and all of that propellant has to be carried onboard. In other words, a rocket has to spend fuel lifting not just its payload, but also the fuel it needs to keep accelerating. This makes getting off Earth an inherently energy-intensive—and expensive—proposition.

With that in mind, engineers continue to explore other ways of getting into space, ideally using less fuel and resources. So far, though, most of their ideas haven’t made it off the drawing board—and, after crunching the numbers, Zhu indicates it’s highly unlikely that trebuchets will ever replace rockets.

“A lot of ideas are fantastical, some are possible, and an even smaller set are economical,” notes Zhu.

Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) brought the case against BYD earlier this year after the Chinese automaker announced that it would launch the car in the United Kingdom in 2027. The preliminary ruling marks a significant setback in BYD’s recent explosive expansion into Europe.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014.

“In these summary proceedings, the preliminary relief judge rules that the Ti7 infringes the EU design of Jaguar Land Rover,” the court mentioned in its November 20 ruling, AN reported. “The characteristic and distinctive elements of the design are reflected in the BYD Ti7.”.

It has been revealed that the Defender is JLR’s best-selling vehicle globally, with the automaker shipping more than 100,000 units last year. Both vehicles have boxy designs with flat rooflights, squared wheel arches, and, notably, body-colored panels in place of the rear side windows.

Unfortunately for JLR, the judge also ruled that the court does not have authority over BYD’s U.K. arm. To that end, JLR is reportedly planning to bring the same claim to the courts in England.

Industry observers note that according to AN, BYD “strongly disagrees” with the ruling and has plans to appeal the result. “The BYD Ti7 is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s rights,” the tech giant said. “We will pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision is incorrect.”.

While the final ruling will likely take some time before it is declared, the Dutch court has prohibited BYD from producing the Ti7 at its upcoming factory in Hungary, where it was due to begin mass production early next year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Trump states he “protected” Elon Musk during his first term, and that “you wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” He tied it to “a certain incident” that he called “a tough incident,” but he didn’t say what it was.
  • Musk had plenty of run-ins with federal regulators between 2017 and 2021.
  • Trump called in to CNBC’s Squawk on the Street on Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Trump states he “protected” Elon Musk during his first term, and that “you wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” He tied it to “a certain incident” that he called “a tough incident,” but he didn’t say what it was.

Musk had plenty of run-ins with federal regulators between 2017 and 2021. One of them could have ended his career as a public company CEO, and it’s our best guess.

Trump called in to CNBC’s Squawk on the Street on Monday. That same morning, Nvidia’s board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, and in its press release it stated it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” before concluding Huang posed no national security risk.

Trump argued that the US needs to “protect our geniuses.” Then he brought up Musk:.

According to recent reports, “You know, I protected Elon in my first term. Very big. Elon was protected. I talk about it, and I’m proud of Elon. I love Elon. I think he’s great. You know, 80% super genius, 20% he has other problems. But I tell him that. But Elon, I protected. You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me. And, you know, a certain incident took place, which was, you know, a tough incident.”.

In a recent development, it’s not the first time he has hinted at it. Last week, in a Fox News interview from Shenzhen, Trump said: “I helped Elon a lot in my first term. I helped him a lot. He was in major trouble.” Back in 2024, he told CNBC he had helped Musk “when I was president,” again without details.

It has been revealed that on August 7, 2018, Musk tweeted that he was “considering taking Tesla private at $420. Funding secured.” It wasn’t. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund had shown interest, but no deal or price had been agreed, and the take-private proposal was dead within three weeks.

It has been revealed that the SEC sued Musk for securities fraud on September 27, 2018. The agency didn’t only ask for a fine. It asked the court to bar Musk from serving as an officer or director of any public company. That would have meant no more Elon at Tesla, which lines up with “you wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me” better than anything else on this list.

According to recent reports, and then it went away fast. Two days later, the SEC revealed a settlement: Musk stayed CEO, gave up the chairman title for three years, and he and Tesla each paid $20 million, $40 million in total. Tesla added two independent directors and agreed to have a lawyer pre-approve Musk’s material tweets, but the SEC never fully enforced it. Musk didn’t admit or deny anything.

The SEC was run at the time by Jay Clayton, a Trump appointee.

There was a criminal side too. In September 2018, federal prosecutors in San Francisco opened a fraud investigation over the same tweet. It never led to charges, and the Justice Department never mentioned publicly why.

Industry observers note that the SEC came back in February 2019 and asked a judge to hold Musk in contempt after he tweeted Tesla production guidance without pre-approval. That one ended in April with an amended deal listing the topics he needed approval for, and no upcoming penalty.

In May 2020, Musk reopened the Fremont factory in defiance of Alameda County’s COVID orders and tweeted: “If anyone is arrested, I ask that it only be me.” Trump tweeted the next day that California “should let Tesla & @elonmusk open the plant, NOW.” But the county was already working toward a reopening date of May 18, and a president doesn’t control county health orders.

According to recent reports, there’s also the September 2018 Joe Rogan episode, where Musk smoked a joint on camera. NASA followed with a workplace safety review of SpaceX and Boeing, and SpaceX lives on federal contracts.

For context, Musk sat on Trump’s business advisory councils early in that first term, and quit in June 2017 when Trump pulled out of the Paris Agreement. That feels like a lifetime ago now that xAI runs its data centers on natural gas turbines.

Our money is on “funding secured.”.

Musk revealed a take-private deal at a specific price that the other side never agreed to, and the stock jumped. It’s textbook securities fraud. The SEC asked to remove him from public company leadership, and two days later he got a $20 million fine, an insignificant amount of money for him, and lost a mostly insignificant title. For someone who’s now worth hundreds of billions, that’s a slap on the wrist.

The main remedy was supposed to be independent oversight. Tesla gave the chair to Robyn Denholm, who had been on the board since 2014, and the board has done what Musk wanted ever since: it defended his pay packages, approved latest ones, and stayed quiet while the brand took damage. Denholm herself has sold tens of millions of dollars in TSLA along the way. The SEC got a governance fix on paper and nothing in practice.

Sources indicate that just imagine where Tesla would be if a product oriented CEO had taken over from Elon in early 2018. The organization would have spent the last 6 years developing upcoming models instead of betting the farm on autonomy. The Cybertruck almost certainly does not happen, at least not in its current form. Instead, they would have developed a more conventional pickup. We'd have gotten 2nd generation models of the X and S instead of them being canceled. Instead of a Cybercab, there would be a model 2 compact car people could buy. And there would likely be a Tesla van and a full sized SUV, possibly developed on the same underlying platform. Also, the SEC was trying to ban him from running public companies. At the time, SpaceX was still private. So, Elon could have still run SpaceX.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that slate made a big splash with its affordable, heavily customizable electric truck. Someone even copied the formula over to a lineup of gas-powered trucks, and we'll see another cheap electric truck from Ford next year. But now the French have their own cheap electric truck concept. It's called the Kilow La Bagnole (which literally translates to "the car"), and it's adorable. I need one.

In a recent development, the La Bagnole is one of the most interesting looking cars I've ever seen, It looks like a French Willy's Jeep but with the fully open wheels of F1 car. It only seats two and two different kinds of body styles, Hard Top (basically a pickup truck) and Closed Hard Top (becomes a van). Both can be had with roof bars so you can put all sorts of gear up there. If you get the Hard Top, the side bed rails are made from either resin-bonded wood fiber or Okoume wood. The former makes it look like it's from IKEA, while the latter looks more premium. However, the Okoume wood requires periodic to keep it weather proof.

According to recent reports, both versions come with an optional removable roof, which is pretty awesome. So you can have either a targa-top pickup or van. The standard La Bagnole lacks doors, and only has substantial metal side bars, but you can option transparent doors, which are neat.

According to recent reports, if you want colors, boy can you get 'em. Kilow offers 12 different regular color options, six gradient colors, and six sparkly "Memories" colors. The best part is that they're all free options. The chassis of the La Bagnole is steel, but all of its body panels are easy removable. So if one breaks or dents, you can just replace it.

Recent findings suggest that there are a few different battery options. Two of the options are made to allow unlicensed drivers to use them. Both the 6 kWh and 12 kWh "Long Range" batteries require no license, as they're classified as quadricycles and capped at 45 km/h (28 mph). Trucks with the 6 kWh battery have only 70 km (43 miles) of range. Cars with the 12 kWh battery can go 164 km (102 miles). The third option mates the 12 kWh battery with an increased speed limiter of 80 km/h (50 mph), but that requires a driver's license.

I love this little thing, and I wish it was coming to the United States. As of right now, it will only be offered in Europe, starting in France. The La Bagnole is such a charming, fun looking little utility vehicle that seems designed equally for function and form. With prices ranging from €10,800 ($11,758) - €13,690 ($14,904), it's an affordable work vehicle for anyone who needs one and stays local, but with tons of character.

Latest Zealand’s Twin-Engine Toyota Celica Is Essentially Unstoppable

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1149 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The art of modifying cars is gleefully rule-free.
  • Industry observers note that wadsworth’s twin-engine Toyota Celica has made literal waves on social video in the past few weeks, as the Christchurch resident demonstrated its remarkable wading abilities in a series of viral videos.
  • With so many moving parts, Wadsworth went analog with the controls; a pulley system attached to the original clutch pedal also operates the clutch for the rear transmission, and the throttle pedal is divided into an upper portion for the front engine and a lower portion for the rear engine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The art of modifying cars is gleefully rule-free. Sure, there are never-ending hoops to jump through for street legality, but actually building your perfect vehicle is merely a matter of dreams. For Kiwi Gareth Wadsworth, who goes by @garethcars on social media, those dreams meant stuffing two engines and two transmissions into a single sixth-generation Toyota Celica. Seems easy enough, right?

Industry observers note that wadsworth’s twin-engine Toyota Celica has made literal waves on social video in the past few weeks, as the Christchurch resident demonstrated its remarkable wading abilities in a series of viral videos. The basic recipe is a pair of Toyota’s 2.0-liter 3S-GE engines—one mounted in the front and one mounted in the rear—mated to a pair of manual transmissions and fed to individual differentials.

With so many moving parts, Wadsworth went analog with the controls; a pulley system attached to the original clutch pedal also operates the clutch for the rear transmission, and the throttle pedal is divided into an upper portion for the front engine and a lower portion for the rear engine. If you press directly in the middle of the accelerator, both engines will rev up (somewhat) in sync. Wadsworth emphasized that it is two completely separate drivetrains that require two of everything (two batteries, two fuel tanks, two ECUs, two radiators) and can be driven separately or simultaneously.

Recent findings suggest that but this Celica build wasn’t always this extreme. In fact, the initial version was supposed to be a simple overlanding setup for a university off-road club trip in 2020. He initially off-roaded the Celica with a simple four-inch lift kit and 31-inch tires, but Wadsworth wanted to try something more extreme—and he didn’t want to abandon the existing platform.

Sources indicate that “I had this Celica that I bought crashed, and I didn't have anything to do with it. I was a student. I didn't have the money for a four-wheel-drive, so I ended up building it into a four-wheel-drive,” Wadsworth stated to Road & Track. “I paid $800 for the car, and then I sold the wheels and tires that were on it. So it was effectively a free car just sitting around, and I got some suspension left over from other projects that I threw in it, and the engine came from a crashed car I found upside down off the side of the road.”.

After a year of mud-slinging fun, Wadsworth decided to go all-in on the dual-engine swap. The rear engine transplant only took two weeks, with most of the work happening after school and during a series of all-nighters. A day or two after the build was complete, Wadsworth and friends trailered the dual-engine Celica to an off-road area and began testing its abilities. Some limitations were quickly revealed.

It has been revealed that “It was just the stock intakes for a few trips. It did have a snorkel on the outside for the front engine. Once it was twin-engine, it had enough power that we could hit the water faster, and that meant that the bow wave would keep going over the roof and filling the front engine's snorkel. We had one trip on the White Bear River that was in flood, and we hydrolocked the front engine twenty-three times, and we got sick of having to pull the spark plugs out, blasting the water out, and trying to get it running again. And so that's why I moved the intake to the glove box,” Wadsworth said.

Wading is one of the twin-engine Celica’s best tricks, as it is fast enough to glide onto the water and light enough to float through. The Celica has floated through currents that have sunk heavier 4x4 trucks, Wadsworth said. But the twin-engine Celica doesn’t just excel at water crossings, either. Because the gearboxes run independently, Wadsworth can tune the gear ratios of either end to suit his needs.

Sources indicate that “There's no weird handling from the differences between the front and rear. It's just whichever engine's got the least load on it speeds up to catch up with the other one. They're effectively a fifty-fifty split,” Wadsworth stated. “Because of the biasing, I quite often run almost exclusively rear-wheel-drive, and I only add front when I need it for traction. It's quite a unique feeling. It's so much fun, and probably the main reason I've still got it is being able to dynamically shift between front, rear, or four-wheel-drive and throttle biasing on the fly. In a mud pit, I can sit around doing donuts with the front in neutral, and then I can put the front-end gear in and let the clutch out slowly on the front to transition from donuts to power slides.”.

Sources indicate that and it isn’t even too hard to drive—relatively speaking. Wadsworth stated that his mates can hop in and romp it with minimal coaching, at least in this configuration. Shifting the two gearboxes can get awkward, but the rear transmission shifter is placed near the traditional shifter, so you don’t have to reach far. Before the pulley clutch system, Wadsworth wired the rear clutch through the parking brake, which required a gentle touch to keep from stalling.

In a recent development, but it wasn’t always so accommodating. “On the original build, we didn't have time to connect any of the controls, so it had two drivers back then. And we didn't have a throttle, so the strap for tightening the hood was tied onto the rearview mirror and back to the rear throttle body, and you pulled it like a train horn,” Wadsworth said. “We certainly had a lot of difficulty driving it when we first built it, because it required two people to communicate—but it didn't have any exhaust, so we couldn't hear each other, and we had no total control on the rear; it was either fully on or fully off. And you had to get up out of your seat, turn around, and put it in gear for the rear engine.”.

Industry observers note that even after six years of ownership and five years with two engines, Wadsworth intends to continue driving the twin-engine Celica as long as possible. Initially, he considered adding four-wheel steering using a power steering motor from a Nissan Leaf, but he mentioned the time under the knife wouldn’t be worth it. The more time spent off-road, the better.

According to recent reports, A Fresh York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

You can browse the full Black Friday tool sale, or jump straight to the lists below, grouped by free-tool promo, brand and category.

Two rules make this sale easier to navigate. First, buying a $99 to $199 battery starter kit with a free tool often costs the same as—or less than—buying that bare tool on its own. Second, watch out for decoy discounts on older brushed drills and mixed bundles that sit right next to newer brushless kits (brushless motors run cooler, last longer and stretch battery runtime). We checked prices and stock at The Home Depot on Wednesday, Nov. 25, ahead of Thanksgiving and Black Friday; pricing and free-tool options can vary by store.

A drill, an impact driver and two batteries for $169.

Sources indicate that A drill/driver and an impact driver cover most of what a homeowner asks of cordless tools, and the DeWalt Atomic 20V Max 2-tool combo kit cuts $80 off a compact entry into DeWalt’s battery system. The bag packs the DCD794 drill/driver, the DCF809 impact driver, two 2.0Ah batteries and a charger—a practical baseline if you’re comparing the best tool combo kits. The brushless impact driver is rated at 1,700 inch-pounds of torque, while the drill’s 5.88-inch head slips easily inside cabinets. Both batteries fit the rest of DeWalt’s 20V Max lineup.

Half off a brushless Milwaukee drill with a battery.

At $99, the Milwaukee M18 brushless 1/2-inch compact drill/driver kit is the cheapest clean on-ramp into Milwaukee’s M18 battery platform. Measuring 5.7 inches front to back, it fits inside cabinets and between joists without forcing awkward angles. Milwaukee rates the motor at 550 inch-pounds of torque and up to 1,700 rpm, and the box includes one 2.0Ah battery, a charger and a soft bag. If you drive more lag bolts and deck screws than you drill holes, grab the matching M18 compact brushless impact driver kit for the same $99 (or check our picks for the best impact drivers).

Two 4.0Ah batteries, a charger and a free tool.

Buy the batteries and the tool comes free. The Ridgid 18V Max Output starter kit pairs two 4.0Ah packs and a charger for $149, and The Home Depot discounts one eligible item in your cart to $0. Standouts on the eight-item menu include a brushless 6-1/2-inch circular saw, a mid-torque impact wrench, an angle grinder, a jigsaw and a 6.0Ah battery. Don’t skip the paperwork after delivery: Ridgid’s Lifetime Service Agreement covers free parts and service on eligible tools bought at The Home Depot, but only if you register them and upload proof of purchase within 90 days.

Level lines across a room for under $50.

Recent findings suggest that hanging a gallery wall or a run of cabinets goes faster with a plumb line already projected across the room. Down to $49.97 from $95, the Bosch GLL50-20 self-leveling cross-line laser casts red horizontal and vertical lines rated out to 50 feet, with an IP55 dust- and water-resistance rating. It runs on included AA batteries (Bosch sells a 3.7V rechargeable pack separately) and mounts via magnets or a 1/4-inch-20 thread (standard camera-tripod mount). Like most red-beam lasers, this model is built strictly for indoor work; step up to a pricier green-beam pick from our guide to the best laser levels if you work in bright, sunlit rooms.

In a recent development, four other brands mirror the Ridgid starter kit above: add the qualifying battery or combo kit to your cart and select a free tool at checkout. The Ryobi ONE+ starter kit is the lowest buy-in at $99, while the $199 DeWalt 20V Max 6.0Ah and 4.0Ah starter kit unlocks 14 free options (check your ZIP code at checkout, as high-value bare tools sell out unevenly by store). A higher amp-hour (Ah) rating means longer runtime—2.0Ah packs keep drills light overhead, while 4.0Ah to 6.0Ah packs keep circular saws and grinders from bogging down.

Milwaukee’s 12V (M12) and 18V (M18) batteries don’t cross over, and anything labeled “tool only” ships without a battery or charger. Fuel marks Milwaukee’s flagship brushless tier, while Packout refers to its interlocking modular toolbox system. Note that the half-off M18 5-tool combo kit ($349) and 9-tool combo kit ($699) are not Fuel sets and mix in older brushed tools—fine for weekend projects, but check the box list if you want all-brushless gear. The M12 4.0Ah battery two-pack also drops to $79, and the $99 M18 drill kit sits near the top of this page.

Don’t scroll past the 20V Max brushless 3-speed oscillating multi-tool kit at $99—getting the tool, a charger and a 4.0Ah battery at half price is one of the quietest steals in this sale. Meanwhile, watch out for the two standalone drills: the $129 20V Max drill/driver kit throws in two tiny 1.3Ah packs, but its DCD771 uses an older brushed motor. Most shoppers are better off spending $30 less on the $99 Atomic compact drill/driver kit, which trades the spare battery for a shorter brushless tool and a higher-capacity 2.0Ah pack (or stepping up to the $169 Atomic 2-tool kit at the top of the page). For decoding DeWalt’s labels below: Atomic is its compact tier, XR is its pro-grade line and FlexVolt packs power both 20V and 60V tools.

Ryobi delivers the lowest kit prices in this roundup, though the cheapest drill deserves a caveat. The $49.97 ONE+ 3/8-inch drill/driver kit tops out at 600 rpm and lacks an adjustable clutch, making it easy to strip screws or overdrive fasteners. Spend $9 more on the ONE+ 1/2-inch drill/driver kit for a two-speed gearbox and real torque control. HP designates Ryobi’s brushless lineup, and if you already own a charger, the $99 4.0Ah battery two-pack is worth weighing against the $99 starter kit plus free tool listed earlier.

Skip the $149 two-battery starter kit if you only need one tool and a single pack: Ridgid’s $99 shelf includes a 4.0Ah battery with the 1/2-inch impact wrench kit, the 6-1/2-inch circular saw kit and the angle grinder kit.

The headline benchtop cut is $200 off the DeWalt DWS780 12-inch sliding miter saw ($449), which uses an LED shadow-line cut indicator instead of a laser you have to recalibrate and tilts both left and right (double-bevel) so you don’t have to flip long trim boards. Note that the two pneumatic nailers below—the $99 DeWalt brad nailer and the $199 Makita AN924 framing nailer (which takes 21-degree plastic-collated nail strips)—require an air compressor and hose sold separately.

If you’re rounding out a latest drill or saw—or grabbing stocking stuffers—consumables start under $10 with the Ryobi 40-piece drill and impact drive kit at $9.97, and the Diablo framing blade two-pack is $12.88.
